summary: A beginner's guide to wok stir-frying that traces the technique to China and covers wok choice and seasoning, heat control, prep, oil selection, movement, sauce timing, the wok toss, and serving immediately. Each section is backed by dated quotes from chefs and instructors at demonstrations, classes, webinars and shows in fall 2023. The guide concludes that with proper equipment, preparation and practice, anyone can make restaurant-quality stir-fries at home.
one_line: A beginner's guide to wok stir-frying covering seasoning, heat, prep, oils, tossing, sauce timing and serving, with chef quotes from 2023.
key_facts: Wok stir-frying is an ancient culinary practice that traces its roots back to the provinces of China.
A good wok is traditionally made from carbon steel, with high walls and a rounded bottom suited to fast, high-heat cooking.
On October 5, 2023, Ken Min said in a San Francisco demonstration that "a well-seasoned carbon steel wok isn't just a cooking vessel; it's a canvas where the stir-frying magic happens."
Seasoning a wok involves heating oil in it to form a protective, non-stick patina over time; Lisa Zhang called seasoning "the soul of your wok" on September 15, 2023.
The wok should be heated until almost smoking before oil and then ingredients are added, which allows the Maillard reaction to give a caramelized exterior and a tender, juicy interior.
Tony Liang, a Colorado-based chef, said on September 20, 2023 that high heat is crucial but the flame must be adjusted to prevent scorching.
Sophie Chan, a Melbourne-based chef, stressed mise en place on September 25, 2023: cut vegetables uniformly and keep sauces and aromatics within reach before the flame is on.
High smoke point oils such as peanut, grapeseed, or canola are ideal; Miguel Torres advised this in a healthy cooking webinar on November 2, 2023.
Swirling and coating the wok with oil is called 'longyau' in Chinese; it prevents sticking and creates a searing hot cooking surface.
Aromatics such as garlic, ginger and scallions should bloom in the hot oil for mere seconds before the main ingredients go in.
Angela Wu said on October 18, 2023 to keep food in constant motion, using a spatula to stir and flip so it cooks evenly without overcooking.
Alex Dima, on the "Morning Culinary Show" on December 1, 2023, advised pushing cooked ingredients aside, reducing the sauce in the center of the wok, then mixing everything together.
Ronald Cheng, a San Diego-based chef instructor, taught on September 30, 2023 to lift the wok slightly off the burner and toss ingredients up and forward with a gentle wrist motion.
Olivia Greene said in an Austin lecture on November 15, 2023 to serve stir-fry straight from the wok to the plate for the best texture and flavor.
